notes: Plan-only evals: a real sdd run dispatches an implementer + reviewer per task and a two-axis final review — an order of magnitude beyond the pipeline budget, so these grade the controller's stated procedure instead. Both prompts assume a repo with a committed plan in a worktree. Assertions in expected_output are behavioral (dispatch discipline, ledger, fix-loop caps, axis separation) rather than quotes of the current SKILL.md prose; contract-sensitive expectations are marked inline with 'contract:'. Grade by pasting the prompt into a session and reading the transcript against the expected output.

evals.name: task-loop-and-fix-loop-discipline
evals.prompt: There's an approved implementation plan with 4 tasks committed in this worktree, and I want you to execute it with the `sdd` skill. **Plan-only for now — dispatch nothing.** Before you start, write out: (1) exactly what the first implementer dispatch will contain and what it will NOT contain; (2) what happens when its task review comes back with one Important finding; (3) what happens if three fix rounds in a row fail; and (4) what you personally are allowed to fix in this session, and why.
evals.expected_output: (1) The dispatch carries a task brief extracted to a file (the brief path is the single source of requirements — contract: briefs are per-task files produced by the skill's task-brief script, matching the thin-index-plus-briefs plan shape), one line of where the task fits, interfaces/decisions from earlier tasks the brief cannot know, the report-file path and contract — and explicitly NOT the whole plan or accumulated prior-task history. BASE is recorded before dispatch for the review package. Implementers are never dispatched in parallel. (2) An Important finding triggers the fix loop: rounds 1-3 resume the SAME implementer with the findings verbatim, each round = one fix dispatch + one scoped re-review (reviewer-lite over the bounded fix diff), and the ledger gets a per-round entry; Minor findings go to the ledger as deferred, never into the loop. (3) Three failed same-context rounds trigger the round-4 stuck-breaker: a bounded external (Codex) diagnosis pass whose result is verified against the live worktree before a fresh Opus/high implementer applies it (fallback: fresh Opus/high implementer with the prior report), then round 5 is the last round; at the cap the controller adjudicates each open finding itself — park with ruling or BLOCKED to the human — and every adjudication is a ledger entry, never a silent discard. (4) The controller fixes nothing in its own session — controller fixes skip review and pollute the coordination context; progress lives in the git-ignored per-plan workspace ledger so the run survives compaction. A response that collapses the fix loop into 'fix and re-review until clean', omits the round cap, lets the controller edit code, or pastes whole-plan text into dispatches is a failure.

evals.name: final-review-two-axes-never-merged
evals.prompt: All tasks in my sdd run are complete and their per-task reviews are clean. Walk me through the final whole-branch review — plan-only, dispatch nothing. Be explicit about: how many reviews run and on what inputs; what each one grades; what you do when both reviews flag the same line; and what states this can end in. Also: the machine this runs on has the codex-collaboration skill installed.
evals.expected_output: One review package built once from MERGE_BASE (git merge-base with the integration branch, not HEAD~1), then TWO isolated reviews in parallel over that same package: a conformance axis (native reviewer — did the diff deliver what issue/spec/plan promised, honoring ADRs and standards; it also triages the ledger's deferred-minor and parked lines) and a correctness axis which, since codex-collaboration is available, goes through that skill's diff-review operation (that skill owns the isolated Codex transport and its one-time native fallback). The two reports are never merged into one narrative — independent signals, dispositioned separately, both verdicts plus the correctness reviewer's identity (Codex | native | fallback) recorded in the ledger — and, because that axis came through diff-review here, the scope it returned recorded alongside (full | scoped: <N> of <M> product files | unmeasured); a native reviewer dispatched directly on the capability fallback returns no scope, so none is recorded in that case. Findings are verified against the live worktree first (stale ones rejected in the ledger), then ONE fixer handles the complete labeled list in one wave — duplicate findings from both axes are deduped at dispatch with both axes credited — followed by exactly one scoped re-review per axis that had findings, over the bounded fix range. No second fix wave: residual load-bearing findings surface to the caller. Terminal states: review_state clean (including everything-parked-with-ruling) with the plan workspace deleted, or review_state residuals with workspace and ledger kept; sdd never reports 'unknown'. Failures: running one blended review, skipping the correctness axis because Codex might time out, per-finding fixer dispatches, merging the axis reports, or shipping/merging (the caller owns delivery).
